paragraphs: Friend, here's what I think Proverbs 17 is really about: what comes out of your mouth and what you do with a hurt will either build up your people or tear them down. Solomon says "Whoever conceals an offense promotes love, but he who brings it up separates friends." (Proverbs 17:9) And he says "To start a quarrel is to release a flood; so abandon the dispute before it breaks out." (Proverbs 17:14) Floods are easy to start and NOT easy to stop, baker.

Then Solomon gives us the kind of person worth being: "A friend loves at all times, and a brother is born for adversity." (Proverbs 17:17) Not a friend for the good days and the free cookies, but one who stays when things get hard. He also says "A joyful heart is good medicine, but a broken spirit dries up the bones." (Proverbs 17:22) I believe the good kind of friend carries some of that medicine with him.

And he ends where we all need the most help, with the mouth. "A man of knowledge restrains his words, and a man of understanding maintains a calm spirit." (Proverbs 17:27) Even a fool looks wise when he holds his tongue (Proverbs 17:28), and friend, I'm preaching to myself on that one. So this week, when you feel a quarrel coming, hold your words, keep your spirit calm and love the people God has put in front of you, at ALL times.
